newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine oil refinery shares to be sold in January.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine oil refinery shares to be sold in January.

text.p: Ukraine plans to put a 45 percent stake in AT Lisichansnaftorsyntez, the country's second-largest oil refinery, up for tender to a strategic investor in January, the chairman of the State Property Fund (FDM) said on Monday.

"The group overseeing the privatisation of the Lisichansk oil refinery will meet in the near future, and will decide on the rules for the tender, which is planned for January of next year," Yuri Yekhanurov told a news conference.
Earlier he said that foreign investors, including Russian companies, were interested in the refinery and that Ukrainian investors were unlikely to be able to fund the purchase.
He said the fund, responsible for privatisation, planned to require the investor to guarantee a certain level of annual output and restructure the refinery's debt.
The company is in bankruptcy hearings, which a Ukrainian court has delayed, in connection with a loan for $70 million, according to the fund, from a German bank.

Earlier Yekhanurov said the refinery, which processed 1.8 million tonnes of crude in the first 10 months of this year, out of an annual capacity of 16 million tonnes, needed to process about six million tonnes per year to break even.
Lisichansk is on a list of more than 200 firms which the government has approved for strategic investment. Investors usually are required to modernise the facilities as well.
Anatoly Mynchenko, state minister in charge of the industrial sector, said last week that an investor could purchase 45 percent of shares from the government, which has a 75.3 percent stake.
Individual investors and refinery workers received a 24.7 percent stake last year.
Ukraine's six oil refineries have an annual capacity of 62 million tonnes, but only refined 16.8 million tonnes in 1995, reflecting a decline in Russian crude oil supplies.
